questions.question: What is a standee line?

options.text: A line passengers must not cross.
A line where passengers should stand.
A line passengers use when exiting the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: A line passengers must not cross.
questions.explanation: On a bus with standing passengers, no one may stand in front of the driver's seat. A line on the floor marks this area. This line is called the standee line.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: Which gas from a faulty exhaust system is dangerous?
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide into the cab. Carbon monoxide is poisonous.

questions.question: In hot weather, what helps keep the engine cool?

options.text: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: In hot weather, check your tire pressure because air expands and pressure increases. Keep enough oil in the engine and enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system. Antifreeze protects the engine in both hot and cold weather.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get a full night's sleep before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a full night's sleep before your trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before a trip. Other strategies include having a passenger with you, driving when you are normally awake, and avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise increases energy and helps prevent tiredness while driving.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do with your turn signal?

options.text: Turn off the signal just before turning.
Signal only if vehicles are ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you turn.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on during the turn. After the turn, turn off the signal if your vehicle does not have self-canceling signals.

questions.question: How does an empty truck compare to a full truck when stopping?

options.text: An empty truck stops in a shorter distance.
An empty truck requires a longer distance to stop.
Both trucks stop in the same distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: An empty truck requires a longer distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need longer to stop because they have less weight and less traction.

questions.question: How can you avoid distracted driving?

options.text: Do not have complex conversations with passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have complex conversations with passengers.
questions.explanation: Distractions include physical activities (reaching for objects), mental activities (talking), or both (holding a phone). To avoid distracted driving, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead, avoid difficult conversations, adjust mirrors before driving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: How should exhaust system parts be maintained?

options.text: They should rub against other parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be secured tightly.
questions.explanation: Check that exhaust system parts are not loose, broken, or missing. All parts must be properly mounted and should not rub against moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if you are unsure if your vehicle fits under a bridge?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under an overhead object, slow down as you approach it. Find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and the car ahead is:

options.text: Not a good idea because it slows traffic.
A good idea because it gives you time to react to problems.
Only important if you have a passenger in your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good idea because it gives you time to react to problems.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires space around all sides of your vehicle. This space gives you time to act if something goes wrong.

questions.question: Black ice is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road shows through it and looks wet. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The ABS light should turn on, then turn off quickly.
The steering wheel will not move until the air tanks are full.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS light should turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start a vehicle with ABS, the indicator light comes on and then goes off. If the light stays on, there is a problem with the ABS.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly toward the floor.
Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the brake pedal three times. Then press hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should stay in place. If it moves, there may be a leak or another brake problem.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are nearby.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during your driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. Poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: To make it easier to leave a parking spot, you should park:

options.text: So you can back up when leaving.
So you can pull forward when leaving.
Only on the side of roads, not in parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward when leaving.
questions.explanation: Backing is always risky and should be avoided when possible. Park in a space that lets you pull forward when you leave.

questions.question: Which of the following shows standing water on the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tire splashes
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen where water collects on the road. Clear reflections, tire splashes, or raindrops on the road show standing water.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a commercial vehicle, the driver should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver.
Not worry about speed, just focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect how slowly your commercial vehicle needs to turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them.

questions.question: ____ are most affected by strong winds.
questions.correctAnswerText: Light vehicles
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. This is especially true for drivers of lighter commercial vehicles.
